svg.title: AI Factory onion V2: API-2-Pipelines
svg.desc: In PROJECT mode the Factory API writes the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's own infra-project pipeline: 13-24 s in the API, 24-52 min in the pipeline. Illustrative animation; every time is measured.

g.text: In PROJECT mode the Factory API writes the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's own infra-project pipeline: 13-24 s in the API,
Same five layers. The API now hands off in seconds.
In PROJECT mode (onion-deployment-mode API-2-Pipelines) the Factory API writes the reviewed configuration and starts the
consumer's own infra-project pipeline. The pipeline does the work. The colours show where the time goes: green is fast, red is the
API: 13-24 s before the pipeline starts. Pipeline: 24-52 min.

text.textPath: L1 · CLIENTS · ESAF FACADE · SDK · CLI

In PROJECT mode the Factory API writes the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's own infra-project pipeline: 13-24 s in the API,
One ESAF call is the approval.
esaf.upsert_project("002", scale_set="002") prepares the review, checks it and confirms it, then returns an EsafJob at once. The client
Fire and forget: job.wait() follows the server-side job to its end.

In PROJECT mode the Factory API writes the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's own infra-project pipeline: 13-24 s in the API,
The API writes the configuration and starts the run.
It installs infra-project.yml when it is missing or differs, hands the project's variables.json to the run as an environment secret, and
starts the run. It no longer freezes an ARM plan or deploys anything itself.
Job created to GitHub run created: 13-24 s (measured 2026-10-31).

In PROJECT mode the Factory API writes the reviewed configuration and starts the consumer's own infra-project pipeline: 13-24 s in the API,
infra-project.yml calls infra-project-phase.yml for networking and services, then AI Foundry, as separate az deployment steps on the
factory's runner. Bicep and ARM time are inside the pipeline's wall clock.
Pipeline wall clock: 24-52 min per PROJECT run.

Enrolling a scale set takes the factory-lifecycle worker route: the API freezes a deployment plan before it starts the pipeline, and the
Worker route: 2 min 18 s in the API before the pipeline, then 10.1 min in it.

Seconds in the API, minutes in the pipeline.
Measured on aif-138 from 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-01. Scenario 6 (delete the factory) is not yet measured.
The API answers in 13-24 s; the pipeline needs 24-52 min.

Where the time goes: minutes per run, by layer
Measured runs on aif-138, stacked by layer: L2 = job created to GitHub run created (Scenario 5: prepare), L3-L5 = the pipeline split by its
step times (R4). Consumer and L1 take seconds. Worker = the factory-lifecycle worker route.
PROJECT path (API-2-Pipelines): Consumer > L1 esaf > L2 writes the configuration and starts the run (13-24 s) > L3 infra-project pipeline > L4 Bicep > L5 (24-52 min)
Worker path (scale-set enroll): L2 freezes a deployment plan (2 min 18 s) > L3 factory-lifecycle worker > L4 Bicep > L5 (10.1 min)
Colours mark the layers, in the rings and in the chart bars: blue Consumer, green L1 Clients, pink L2 Factory REST API, purple L3 Pipelines, orange L4 Bicep +
pipeline-called scripts, red L5 Azure Resource Manager.
